claim: A multiplicatively weighted center, optimum value, and all centers of any finite unweighted median graph can be computed deterministically in O(n log^5(2n)) exact-arithmetic/comparison operations.
model: Finite nonempty connected simple median graph in adjacency-list form; unit edge lengths; nonnegative finite vertex weights; exact comparisons of small-integer multiples of input weights.
mechanism: Threshold feasibility reduces to additive eccentricities with integer weights in [0,n-1]; weighted-median pruning searches n implicit sorted rows in O(log n) oracle calls.

imported_theorem.scope: All nonnegative integer additive eccentricities on finite median graphs in O(n log^4 n).

novelty: Not certified. The theorem is a short consequence of existing algorithmic tools and the threshold transformation. No source explicitly stating this exact consequence was located in the bounded search.
remaining_mathematical_gap: None claimed within the stated model, assuming the cited published additive-eccentricity theorem. Independent verification remains pending.
control_limits: The general additive oracle in controls is quadratic reference code. A separate fast tree oracle is tested. No implementation or benchmark of BDH is supplied.
